title: Hereditarily small sets: hereditary cardinality

based_on.title: An Introduction to Set Theory
based_on.pages: 101–102 (Theorem 41, Exercise 34, and the finite case of Theorem 42)

summary: Hereditary size bounds membership rank and defines transitive sets closed under suitably small set formation.
abstract: A singleton has just one member, but that member may be an uncountable set. Hereditary cardinality counts the set itself, its members, their members, and everything reached by continuing in this way. Under the axiom of choice, requiring this total to be smaller than a given infinite cardinal produces a transitive set of hereditarily small sets, containing the members of each of its elements. The hereditarily countable sets include every subset of the natural numbers but exclude the set of all those subsets. A countable collection of hereditarily countable sets is again hereditarily countable, even though taking a power set need not preserve this property.
